summary: Refined system architecture by integrating probabilistic data structures (Bloom filters, HMMs, Bayesian inference) for telemetry and implementing complexity-aware scheduling to mitigate NP-hard performance risks. These efforts established a robust framework for resource-aware execution, semantic cache integrity, and structural growth measured against the 1% architectural output metric.
key_learnings: Layering probabilistic filters (Bloom filters, HMMs) before deterministic logic optimizes system throughput and reduces semantic search overhead.
Greedy heuristics and complexity-aware guardrails are essential for managing NP-hard resource scheduling without production-level performance collapses.
Semantic cache drift is effectively mitigated through normalized hashing and identity validation.
Architectural progress is best tracked by focusing the 1% growth metric on structural output rather than general task completion.
